timelineEvents.title: Arrival in New York en route to Los Angeles
timelineEvents.label: 24 Oct 1934 · Arrival in New York
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Kaper arrives in New York from France with Eleonora, holding a temporary visa and travelling onward to Los Angeles.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Kaper and his wife Eleonora arrived in New York aboard the S.S. Champlain from Le Havre on 24 October 1934, with Los Angeles listed as their destination.

timelineEvents.title: Duke Ellington records “All God’s Chillun Got Rhythm”
timelineEvents.label: 8 Jun 1937 · Ellington records “All God’s Chillun Got Rhythm”
timelineEvents.shortDescription: Duke Ellington and His Famous Orchestra record “All God’s Chillun Got Rhythm” in New York, carrying a Kaper–Jurmann film song into the jazz repertoire.
timelineEvents.longDescription: Duke Ellington and His Famous Orchestra recorded “All God’s Chillun Got Rhythm” in New York on 8 June 1937 for Master (MA 137, matrix M 519-1). Written by Bronisław Kaper and Walter Jurmann with words by Gus Kahn for A Day at the Races, the song passed from the screen into the jazz repertoire within weeks of the film’s release.

places.publicNote: Arrival city for Kaper and Eleonora after the transatlantic crossing from Le Havre aboard the S.S. Champlain, before onward travel to Los Angeles.
